hook.text: Two users read the same bank balance at the same time. One withdraws $100. What does the other see?

buildup.text: Isolation levels control what concurrent transactions can see. Higher isolation means fewer anomalies.

discovery.text: Read Committed prevents dirty reads. Repeatable Read prevents phantom reads. Serializable prevents everything.

twist.text: Serializable is the safest but slowest. Most databases default to Read Committed for performance.

climax.text: Choosing the right isolation level is a trade-off between correctness and concurrency.

punchline.text: Higher isolation, fewer bugs — but less throughput.

quiz.question: What does the Serializable isolation level guarantee?
options: Transactions behave as if executed one at a time
